backlog.spec: In featurize, compute the full RDKit descriptor set (rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors or the Descriptors._descList loop) for each molecule, replace NaN/inf with 0, clip extreme values to the 1st-99th percentile of the training set, and hstack these columns onto the 2048-bit Morgan array before fitting the same RandomForestRegressor. Compute the clipping bounds from train_smiles only.
backlog.title: Add RDKit 2D physchem descriptors to Morgan bits

backlog.spec: Build a compact feature vector of about 12 Caco-2-relevant descriptors: TPSA, MolLogP, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, NumAromaticRings, RingCount, FractionCSP3, HeavyAtomCount, number of formal charges, and count of carboxylic acid groups (SMARTS C(=O)[OH]). Fit a RandomForestRegressor on these descriptors alone, with the same tree settings as the incumbent, to test whether a low-dimensional physically meaningful space generalizes better across scaffolds.
backlog.title: Curated small physchem descriptor set for a tree model

backlog.spec: Replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy using the same radius-2 generator and 2048 size, so each feature is the number of times each substructure occurs. Keep the RandomForestRegressor unchanged. Count features often carry more information than presence/absence bits for property regression.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints instead of bit vectors

backlog.spec: Build the Morgan generator with the feature-invariant atom invariants (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=2048, atomInvariantsGenerator=GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen())) so atoms are typed by pharmacophoric role (donor, acceptor, aromatic, halogen) rather than element. Use the count variant and the unchanged RandomForest. This generalizes better across unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Feature-Morgan (FCFP-style) fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute hashed atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 1024) and topological-torsion count fingerprints (GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator, fpSize 1024) for each molecule, hstack them with the 2048-bit Morgan features, and fit the same random forest. This adds non-local topology information that scaffold-split generalization may need.
backlog.title: Concatenate atom-pair and torsion count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute the 167-bit MACCS structural keys with rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys for each molecule and hstack them onto the Morgan bit vector before fitting the random forest. MACCS keys encode broad functional-group presence and are a cheap complementary view.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys to the fingerprint

backlog.spec: Add a small block of counts from SMARTS patterns that matter for membrane permeation: carboxylic acid, primary/secondary/tertiary aliphatic amine, quaternary nitrogen, sulfonic/phosphate acid, amide bond, hydroxyl, and halogen count. Append these integer counts to the Morgan features before fitting the random forest. Caco-2 permeability is strongly governed by ionization state and polar groups.
backlog.title: Ionization and polarity SMARTS features

backlog.spec: Before computing any features, apply rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize (Uncharger neutralization and LargestFragmentChooser, with salt stripping) to each SMILES, falling back to the raw molecule if standardization fails. Use the standardized molecules for all fingerprints and descriptors in both train and test. This removes salt and counterion noise that inflates feature variance.
backlog.title: Standardize molecules before featurizing

backlog.spec: Compute the Bemis-Murcko scaffold of every training molecule, count how many training molecules share each scaffold, and pass sample_weight = 1/sqrt(count) to RandomForestRegressor.fit. This prevents large scaffold families from dominating the trees and tends to help generalization to unseen skeletons.
backlog.title: Sample weights that down-weight over-represented scaffolds

backlog.spec: Before fitting, clip train_y to its 2nd and 98th percentiles computed from train_y only, then fit the unchanged random forest on the clipped target and predict test molecules. Outlier measurements inflate the squared-error split criterion, and clipping reduces their pull on the leaves while leaving the bulk of the data unchanged.
backlog.title: Winsorize training targets

backlog.spec: Keep the fitted RandomForestRegressor, but instead of model.predict, stack the predictions of each individual tree in model.estimators_ for the test molecules and return the per-molecule median across trees. Since the metric is mean absolute error, the median of the tree ensemble is the better point estimate than the mean.
backlog.title: Median-of-trees prediction for MAE

backlog.spec: Use RandomForestRegressor(criterion='absolute_error') with a reduced tree count (about 100) so the fit fits the 10-minute budget, keeping max_features 0.3 and the Morgan features. Splits then optimize the same L1 loss the harness scores. Check the wall-clock time carefully, since the absolute-error criterion is much slower than squared error.
backlog.title: Random forest with absolute-error criterion

backlog.spec: Build features as Morgan counts concatenated with RDKit 2D descriptors (NaN to 0, clipped). Train lightgbm.LGBMRegressor with objective='l1', n_estimators about 600, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 31, subsample 0.8 with subsample_freq 1, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_samples 10, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8. Gradient boosting with an L1 objective directly targets the median, matching the MAE metric.
backlog.title: LightGBM with L1 objective on fingerprints plus descriptors

backlog.spec: Use xgboost.XGBRegressor with objective='reg:absoluteerror', tree_method='hist', max_depth 6, learning_rate 0.03, n_estimators 600, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_weight 3, random_state=seed, on Morgan count features concatenated with RDKit 2D descriptors. Compare as an alternate boosting implementation for the same L1 target.
backlog.title: XGBoost with absolute-error objective

backlog.spec: Train catboost.CatBoostRegressor(loss_function='MAE', iterations 1000, learning_rate 0.05, depth 6, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8) on RDKit 2D descriptors plus a 1024-bit Morgan bit vector. CatBoost's symmetric trees are strongly regularized and often perform well on small tabular data like this 728-molecule set.
backlog.title: CatBoost with MAE loss on descriptors

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto (Jaccard on bit vectors, or min/max on count vectors) similarity matrix between training molecules, and between test and training molecules, using the Morgan bit fingerprints. Fit sklearn.svm.SVR with kernel='precomputed', C about 10, epsilon 0.05, on the training kernel and predict with the test-versus-train kernel. Tanimoto kernels are the standard chemically sensible similarity for fingerprint regression.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel support vector regression

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto similarity kernel on Morgan bit fingerprints (K(a,b)=|a AND b|/(|a|+|b|-|a AND b|)). Fit sklearn.kernel_ridge.KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha around 0.3) on the centered training targets (subtract the training mean, add it back at prediction). Predict test molecules from the test-by-train kernel. Kernel ridge on Tanimoto is a smooth, low-variance baseline.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Compute Tanimoto similarities between test and training Morgan bit fingerprints. For each test molecule, take the k=7 most similar training molecules and predict the similarity-weighted median (or weighted mean with weights sim^3) of their targets. Nearest-neighbour regression is a strong, simple baseline for activity-style data and gives a diverse model for blending.
backlog.title: Similarity-weighted k-nearest-neighbour regression

backlog.spec: Fit the incumbent random forest on Morgan bits and a LightGBM model with L1 objective on Morgan counts plus RDKit descriptors, then return the simple average of the two test predictions. Averaging two differently biased learners usually lowers MAE more than tuning either one alone.
backlog.title: Blend random forest and gradient boosting

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run an inner 5-fold KFold (shuffle=True, random_state=seed) on the training molecules to produce out-of-fold predictions from three base models: the random forest on Morgan bits, a Tanimoto-kernel SVR, and a LightGBM model with L1 objective on descriptors. Fit a non-negative linear regression (sklearn LinearRegression(positive=True)) on those OOF predictions, then refit the base models on all training data and combine their test predictions with the learned weights.
backlog.title: Stacked ridge meta-learner over diverse base models

backlog.spec: Fit the random forest on Morgan features as in the incumbent, compute out-of-bag predictions (oob_score=True, or use the model's oob_prediction_), take residuals y - oob, and fit a LightGBM regressor with L1 objective on RDKit 2D descriptors to predict those residuals. Final prediction is RF test prediction plus the residual model's test prediction. This lets the descriptor model correct systematic RF bias.
backlog.title: Residual boosting on top of the random forest

backlog.spec: Keep the Morgan bit features and the random forest, but set min_samples_leaf to 3 and max_features to 0.15 (or sqrt of the feature count), and cap max_depth at 20. Larger leaves and fewer features per split reduce variance on the small, scaffold-shifted training sets. Only these three settings change.
backlog.title: Tune random forest regularization: leaf size and feature fraction

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators 500, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 2, n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed) on Morgan counts concatenated with RDKit 2D descriptors. Extra-randomized splits give smoother predictions and reduce variance, which can help when test scaffolds are unseen.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees on combined features

backlog.spec: Train LightGBM with objective='l1' on RDKit descriptors plus Morgan counts, and set monotone_constraints so that TPSA and NumHDonors have a non-increasing effect on predicted log permeability (constraint -1 on those columns, 0 elsewhere). Permeability is known to fall with polarity, so a monotone prior removes spurious non-physical splits and regularizes the model.
backlog.title: Monotone constraints on polarity descriptors in LightGBM

backlog.spec: Build RDKit 2D descriptors (NaN to 0, clipped to training percentiles), standardize with a StandardScaler fit on the training set, and fit sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor(hidden_layer_sizes=(256,128), alpha=1e-2 for L2 weight decay, learning_rate_init 1e-3, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction 0.15, max_iter 500, random_state=seed). Scale the target by its training standard deviation before fitting and invert after prediction.
backlog.title: MLP on standardized descriptors with weight decay

backlog.spec: Split the training molecules into 4 folds using GroupKFold with Bemis-Murcko scaffold labels as groups, then train LightGBM with objective='l1' on each inner split with early stopping (patience 50, metric 'l1') to find the best iteration count. Average those best iteration counts and retrain on all training data with that many rounds. Tuning the stopping point on scaffold-held-out data matches the evaluation protocol.
backlog.title: Inner scaffold-group CV to choose the number of boosting rounds

backlog.spec: For LightGBM with objective='l1' on Morgan counts plus RDKit descriptors, use learning_rate 0.01 with n_estimators 2000, subsample 0.7 (subsample_freq 1), colsample_bytree 0.2, and lambda_l2 2.0. Slower shrinkage with stochastic row and column sampling typically finds a smoother minimum than a few large steps on small data.
backlog.title: Low learning rate with many boosting rounds and strong subsampling

backlog.spec: Set RandomForestRegressor(bootstrap=True, max_samples=0.6, n_estimators 1000, max_features 0.3, n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed) so each tree sees a 60 percent subsample of the molecules. Smaller bootstrap samples decorrelate trees more strongly, which lowers variance when the training set is small and scaffolds are split by group.
backlog.title: Bagged random forests with row subsampling

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, train 5 random forests (or LightGBM models) with seeds seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4, each on a random 85 percent subsample of the training molecules drawn with a seeded RandomState, and return the mean of their test predictions. Averaging over bootstrap-style subsamples reduces prediction variance without changing the base learner.
backlog.title: Average over several seeds and fold-bootstrap models

backlog.spec: Build three feature views: Morgan bits radius 2, feature-Morgan counts, and MACCS keys. Fit one RandomForestRegressor per view (300 trees each, max_features 0.3, same seed) and average their test predictions with equal weights. Combining models trained on different chemical representations gives complementary errors.
backlog.title: Per-fingerprint random forest ensemble

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, change the XGBRegressor objective from 'reg:absoluteerror' to 'reg:pseudohubererror' and set huber_slope to about 0.5 (the target is on a log scale, so residuals are mostly under 1). Keep every other setting, including the 600 rounds and learning_rate 0.03. The loss is still MAE, so the model is compared on the same metric. Use only the seed argument for randomness.
backlog.title: Pseudo-Huber objective in XGBoost

backlog.spec: Switch XGBoost to booster='dart' with rate_drop around 0.1, skip_drop around 0.5, and sample_type='uniform'. Keep reg:absoluteerror, max_depth 6, colsample_bytree 0.3, and subsample 0.8. Because DART is slower, raise the learning rate to about 0.05 and drop n_estimators to about 400. Predict with the default weights. Keep the seed argument as the only source of randomness.
backlog.title: DART booster for dropout-style regularization

backlog.spec: Fit a ridge regression first on a small standardized set of physchem descriptors (TPSA, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, MolWt, NumRotatableBonds, fraction aromatic atoms). Compute the training residuals, then fit the existing XGBoost L1 model on Morgan counts plus all descriptors to those residuals. The prediction is the ridge output plus the XGBoost output on the test molecules. Caco-2 permeability is known to be close to linear in TPSA and H-bond count, so the trees only need to model the leftover structure.
backlog.title: Linear physchem baseline with boosted residuals

backlog.spec: Add a block of 3D shape features to the existing feature vector. For each molecule, add explicit hydrogens, embed one conformer with a fixed random seed derived from the seed argument (AllChem.EmbedMolecule with randomSeed), and optimize it with MMFF when that works. Compute rdMolDescriptors.CalcPBF, CalcPMI1, CalcPMI2, CalcPMI3, CalcNPR1, CalcNPR2, CalcRadiusOfGyration, and CalcInertialShapeFactor. Set the values to 0 when embedding fails. Cache by SMILES as the code already does. Concatenate these with the current features and keep the XGBoost L1 model unchanged.
backlog.title: 3D shape descriptors from ETKDG conformers

backlog.spec: Add a count-based 2D pharmacophore fingerprint to the features. Use rdkit.Chem.Pharm2D.Gobbi_Pharm2D.factory with rdkit.Chem.Pharm2D.Generate.Gen2DFingerprint, which gives a fixed-length bit vector. Convert it to a numpy array and concatenate it with the existing Morgan counts and descriptors. Fingerprints over 2048 bits can be reduced by keeping only the columns that are set in at least 2% of training molecules. Choose the feature set inside fit_predict using training molecules only, so no test information is used. Leave the XGBoost L1 model as it is.
backlog.title: Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprints

backlog.spec: Run a two-round self-training procedure inside fit_predict. First fit the current XGBoost L1 model on the training molecules and predict the test molecules. Then append the test molecules with those predicted values to the training set, using a weight of 0.5, and refit the same model with the same seed. Return the second-round predictions for the test molecules. This adapts the trees to the unseen scaffolds in the test fold. Use only the seed argument for randomness.
backlog.title: Transductive pseudo-labelling on test molecules

backlog.spec: Replace the tree model with a GP. Apply sklearn QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal') fit on training descriptors only to the RDKit physchem descriptors, dropping columns with zero variance. Use sklearn GaussianProcessRegressor with kernel ConstantKernel * RBF(length_scale=1.0 per feature, or a single shared length scale) + WhiteKernel, normalize_y=True, and n_restarts_optimizer=2 with random_state=seed. Predict the test molecules' posterior means. Fitting should take a few seconds on about 600 molecules. Keep only the predictive mean.
backlog.title: Gaussian process regression on quantile-transformed descriptors

backlog.spec: Before fitting, remove every Morgan count column (and every descriptor column) that is non-zero in fewer than 1% of training molecules. Use the training data to decide which columns to keep, and apply the same mask to the test molecules. In XGBoost, replace colsample_bytree=0.3 with colsample_bynode=0.3 and set colsample_bytree=1.0. This tests whether removing noisy rare bits and sampling per split instead of per tree improves generalization. Keep all other settings.
backlog.title: Drop sparse fingerprint bits with per-node column sampling

backlog.spec: Before training, transform the training targets with sklearn QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal', n_quantiles=min(len(y), 200)) fit on train_y only. Fit the existing XGBoost L1 model on the transformed targets, predict the test molecules, and map the predictions back with inverse_transform. This makes the target distribution closer to Gaussian, which can help the trees reach the tails, and it leaves the MAE scoring unchanged because the inverse mapping is monotone. Keep the model settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Rank-Gaussian target transform with inverse mapping

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, train B=8 XGBoost L1 models. Each one uses a bootstrap sample of the training molecules drawn by sampling unique Murcko scaffold groups with replacement (use rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold on the training SMILES), so the bags follow the scaffold structure that the harness uses. Give each model its own seed derived from the seed argument. Predict the test molecules with each model and return the element-wise median across the B predictions. The median suits MAE and the bags reduce variance. Keep the per-model XGBoost settings but use n_estimators=400 to stay within the time limit.
backlog.title: Scaffold-bagged XGBoost ensemble with median aggregation

backlog.spec: Keep the current XGBoost L1 model. Inside fit_predict, run an inner 5-fold split on the training molecules (KFold with shuffle, seeded). Fit the XGBoost model in each inner fold and collect out-of-fold predictions for all training molecules. Fit a two-parameter map y ~ a*p + b by minimising MAE over those out-of-fold predictions (scipy.optimize.minimize on the absolute error, starting from a=1, b=0). Train the final XGBoost model on all training data, predict the test molecules, and return a*pred + b. Tree ensembles shrink predictions toward the mean, so this should undo some of that shrinkage. Keep the inner loop to the same hyperparameters.
backlog.title: Linear stretch calibration of out-of-fold predictions

backlog.spec: Keep the Morgan count plus RDKit descriptor features and the XGBoost L1 model. Add a block of ring-topology features computed per molecule: the Murcko scaffold hashed into 256 bits with rdFingerprintGenerator (or a hashed fingerprint of each ring system's SMILES), the number of ring systems, the number of rings per size (3 to 8), the fraction of ring atoms, and the fraction of sp3 atoms. Concatenate these to the existing vector and cache them in _CACHE like the other features. Nothing else changes. The aim is to let the trees separate molecules by the ring framework that the scaffold split holds out.
backlog.title: Ring-system and scaffold-topology features

backlog.spec: Keep the Morgan count plus RDKit descriptor vector and the XGBoost L1 model. Append two more fingerprints per molecule, both cached per SMILES: the Avalon count fingerprint (rdkit.Avalon pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP at 512 bits, or the bit version if the count version is unavailable) and the ErG reduced-graph pharmacophore fingerprint (rdkit.Chem.rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint, 315 floats). Concatenate them after the existing features. Use colsample_bytree=0.3 as before. Guard each call with try/except so that a failed fingerprint returns zeros of the correct length, so a single bad molecule cannot crash the job.
backlog.title: Avalon and ErG fingerprints appended to Morgan counts

backlog.spec: Replace reg:absoluteerror with a custom XGBoost objective that is smooth near zero and robust in the tails: a Cauchy or Fair loss with scale c set to 1.0 times the median absolute deviation of the training targets. Define the gradient and Hessian as functions of the residual r = prediction - y: for the Cauchy loss, grad = 2r/(c^2+r^2) and hess = 2(c^2 - r^2)/(c^2+r^2)^2, clipped below at 1e-3 so the Hessian stays positive. Pass it as obj= in XGBRegressor (or the train API) and keep all other hyperparameters. Compare against the pure L1 incumbent, since L1 has a constant Hessian and may be a poor fit for second-order tree splits.
backlog.title: Custom smooth-L1 (Cauchy) objective in XGBoost

backlog.spec: Keep the XGBoost L1 model and its features, but change the learning rate over the boosting rounds. Start at 0.06 and decay with a cosine schedule to 0.003 at the final round, which is 800 rounds. Implement it with an xgboost.callback.LearningRateScheduler (or by updating the learning_rate parameter each round in a train loop with xgb.train). Use the seed for all randomness. Keep subsample=0.8 and colsample_bytree=0.3. The point is to take large steps early and fine-grained steps late, which the constant learning rate does not do.
backlog.title: Cosine learning-rate decay inside boosting

backlog.spec: Replace the single XGBoost model with a small ensemble of 6 XGBoost L1 models that differ in hyperparameters and seed. Use max_depth in {4, 6, 8} and colsample_bytree in {0.2, 0.5} in a fixed grid, each with a different seed derived from the seed argument, and n_estimators scaled so that each model uses about the same total work. Predict on the test molecules with each model and return the element-wise median across the 6 predictions. The median is consistent with an L1 objective, and the mixed depths and column rates diversify the errors. Keep the feature set unchanged.
backlog.title: Hyperparameter-diverse XGBoost ensemble with median aggregation

backlog.spec: Before fitting, replace each training target with a blend of its measured value and the mean target of its k nearest training neighbours under Tanimoto similarity on Morgan bits (k=5, excluding itself, computed inside the training fold only). Use y_train_used = (1 - lam) * y + lam * knn_mean with lam = 0.2. Fit the unchanged XGBoost L1 model on y_train_used and predict the test molecules as usual. The shrinkage works as a regularizer that damps label noise. Use a single fixed lam, and compute the neighbour means with numpy on binary fingerprints so the cost stays small.
backlog.title: Target denoising toward nearest-neighbour means

backlog.spec: Split the training targets at their median. Train an XGBoost binary classifier (objective binary:logistic, same features and depth-6 settings) to predict whether a molecule is above the median. Train two XGBoost L1 regressors, one on the below-median molecules and one on the above-median molecules. For each test molecule, compute the classifier probability q and return q * pred_high + (1 - q) * pred_low. This mixture lets each regime be fit separately, while the soft weights keep the output continuous and avoid hard errors at the boundary. Keep the seed on all three models.
backlog.title: Two-stage hurdle: classifier-weighted regressors

backlog.spec: Keep the XGBoost L1 model as the base predictor. Inside fit_predict, run an inner 5-fold split on the training molecules to get out-of-fold XGBoost predictions and their residuals r = y - p. For each test molecule, find its k=10 nearest training molecules by Tanimoto similarity on Morgan bits, and add the median of their out-of-fold residuals, weighted by similarity, to the base prediction. Use a shrinkage factor of 0.5 on the correction. This adds a local, similarity-based fix to the global tree model, so it targets the residual structure that scaffold-split folds leave behind. Use numpy for the similarity computation.
backlog.title: kNN residual correction of XGBoost predictions

backlog.spec: Build 4 Morgan count fingerprints of radius 2, each folded to 512 bits with a different bit-hash salt (for example by modding the unfolded feature IDs by 512 after offsetting them with a salt that depends on the view index). Train one XGBoost L1 model on each view plus the RDKit descriptor vector, with a different seed for each view. Average the 4 predictions for the test molecules. The folded views keep the feature count small per model but use different collision patterns, so the views disagree in useful ways. Keep depth 6, learning_rate 0.03 and n_estimators 600 for each view.
backlog.title: Hash-folded fingerprint views with bagged XGBoost

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace the Ridge(alpha=1.0) baseline on the standardized 7 physchem features (TPSA, MolLogP, HBD, HBA, MolWt, rotatable bonds, aromatic fraction) with a least-absolute-deviation linear fit, e.g. sklearn QuantileRegressor(quantile=0.5, alpha=0.0, solver='highs') or an IRLS loop with weights 1/max(|r|,0.01). Everything else stays: the XGBoost L1 model is fit on y minus this baseline, and the baseline is added back at prediction. Rationale: the metric is MAE, and an L2 baseline is pulled by outliers, so the residual target the trees see is distorted.
backlog.title: Median-regression (L1) physchem baseline instead of Ridge

backlog.spec: Before fitting the XGBoost L1 residual model, augment the training set: stack 3 copies of the feature matrix, and in each copy set a random 20% of the Morgan count columns to zero (keep the RDKit descriptor columns untouched), with the same residual target repeated. Draw the masks from np.random.default_rng(seed) so the run is reproducible. Increase n_estimators proportionally only if needed (keep it at 600 first). This acts as input-noise regularization on the sparse fingerprint, which the current model fits almost deterministically.
backlog.title: Bit-dropout row augmentation for the XGBoost residual model

backlog.spec: Compute, for each test molecule, its maximum Tanimoto similarity to the training molecules on Morgan bit fingerprints (BulkTanimotoSimilarity). Define a gate g = clip((sim - 0.3) / 0.3, 0, 1). Final prediction = g * model_prediction + (1 - g) * median(train_y). Molecules with no close training analogue, where the model extrapolates from unrelated scaffolds, are pulled toward the central value that minimises MAE for an unknown target. Choose the thresholds 0.3 and 0.6 once and do not tune them further.
backlog.title: Similarity-gated shrinkage toward the training median for out-of-domain molecules

backlog.spec: Replace the residual model with a pairwise learner. For training, sample about 20000 random pairs (i, j) from the training set (seeded). Build the pair feature as the difference x_i - x_j on the standardized descriptor-plus-count features, with target y_i - y_j, and fit an XGBoost regressor with reg:absoluteerror on the pair set; to keep the sign symmetric, include both (i,j) and (j,i). At prediction time, for each test molecule t, average over K=50 random training anchors a the value y_a + f(x_t - x_a), where f is the fitted pair model. Return the mean over anchors, and keep the physchem ridge baseline out of this path. This is a bold change: it turns regression into a learned relative-ranking model that is anchored to the training labels.
backlog.title: Pairwise-difference model with anchor averaging

backlog.spec: Replace the physchem ridge base with a sparse linear median regression on all RDKit descriptors (Descriptors.descList, nan-cleaned, clipped, then standardized using training statistics only). Fit sklearn QuantileRegressor(quantile=0.5, alpha=0.01, solver='highs') on the training fold, using the training-set standardization. Use its predictions as the base, then fit the existing XGBoost L1 model on the residual of the Morgan count plus descriptor features. The L1 penalty zeroes out most descriptors, so the base is an interpretable median model rather than an L2 fit over many collinear features.
backlog.title: Sparse L1 median regression on the full RDKit descriptor set as the base model

backlog.spec: Compute kernel density estimates of the training molecules in the standardized 7-dimensional physchem space (Gaussian kernel, bandwidth set by Scott's rule on the training set only). Give each training molecule sample weight w_i proportional to 1/density_i, clipped to the range [0.2, 5] and normalized to mean 1. Pass these weights to the XGBoost fit (sample_weight=w). The aim is to stop the dense, drug-like region of property space from dominating the tree splits while the sparse, extreme-permeability molecules are under-weighted. The baseline fit is left unweighted.
backlog.title: Density-based sample reweighting in physchem space

backlog.spec: Build the Morgan count matrix for the union of train and test molecules (unlabelled test rows are allowed here since only features are used). Fit sklearn TruncatedSVD(n_components=32, random_state=seed) on the union, optionally after a log1p transform of the counts. Append the 32 latent components to the feature matrix used by the XGBoost L1 residual model, alongside the existing Morgan counts and RDKit descriptors. Only the features are shared across the boundary; no labels are used. This gives the trees a dense, smooth axis of chemical-space position that the sparse bits lack.
backlog.title: Transductive truncated-SVD embedding of the fingerprint matrix

backlog.spec: Fit the XGBoost residual model in two stages on the same features. Stage 1: objective='reg:squarederror' for 200 rounds at learning_rate 0.03, which gives a fast, smooth fit. Stage 2: continue training from that booster with objective='reg:absoluteerror' for the remaining 400 rounds (use xgb.train with xgb_model= the stage-1 booster, or the XGBoost sklearn API with xgb_model=). The L2 phase finds the broad structure, and the L1 phase refines the median-targeted fit. Keep all other hyperparameters as in the incumbent.
backlog.title: Two-stage annealing from L2 to L1 boosting

backlog.spec: Train the XGBoost L1 residual model once for 900 rounds at the incumbent learning_rate 0.03. Make predictions for the test set at three checkpoints, using the iteration_range argument of predict: rounds 400, 600 and 900 (iteration_range=(0,k)). Return the mean of the three predictions on the residual scale, added to the baseline. This is a free ensemble that smooths over the choice of the round count without extra training cost, and does not require inner validation.
backlog.title: Snapshot averaging over boosting rounds

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, produce an inner 5-fold out-of-fold prediction for the training set using the same model, grouping folds by Murcko scaffold (GroupKFold on the scaffold SMILES). Sort the OOF predictions into 10 quantile bins. For each bin, store the median of (y - oof_prediction). At test time, add to each test prediction the stored median correction of the bin it falls into (use np.searchsorted on the bin edges, clipping at the ends). This is a nonlinear, median-based calibration. It is different from the earlier linear stretch, which was a global affine fit, and it targets the prediction-dependent bias of the L1 model.
backlog.title: Binned median correction of predictions learned from out-of-fold residuals

backlog.spec: Replace the single L1 XGBoost residual model with a classifier over target quantile bins. Inside fit_predict, compute 20 quantile edges of the residual target y - base_tr from the training set and assign each training molecule to its bin. Fit XGBClassifier(objective='multi:softprob', n_estimators about 300, max_depth 4, learning_rate 0.05, colsample_bytree 0.3, subsample 0.8, random_state=seed) on featurize(train_smiles). For each test molecule, take the predicted bin probabilities, build the CDF over bin midpoints, and return the value where the CDF crosses 0.5 (linearly interpolated), added to base_te. Keep the Ridge physchem base unchanged.
backlog.title: Distributional median via quantile-bin multiclass XGBoost

backlog.spec: Before fitting the XGBoost L1 residual model, augment the training set with convex combinations of random training pairs. For each seed, draw about 0.5 times n_train pairs (i, j) with lambda from Beta(0.4, 0.4) and build X = lambda*X_i + (1-lambda)*X_j and residual target = lambda*r_i + (1-lambda)*r_j, where r is y minus the physchem ridge base. Concatenate the augmented rows with the originals and fit the same XGBRegressor(reg:absoluteerror). Use the seed argument for all sampling. Predict on unmodified test features and add base_te as before.
backlog.title: Mixup augmentation for the boosted residual model

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, first fit the current model with an inner 4-fold KFold on the training molecules (shuffled with seed) to get out-of-fold residuals of y minus base. Drop the 5 percent of training molecules with the largest absolute out-of-fold residual as likely label noise. Refit the physchem Ridge base and the XGBoost L1 residual model on the remaining 95 percent, then predict the test set with the refit models. Do not change any other settings.
backlog.title: Trimmed refit after out-of-fold residual screening

backlog.spec: Estimate the density of the training targets y with a 1-D Gaussian KDE (scipy.stats.gaussian_kde, bandwidth from Scott's rule). Set each molecule's sample weight to the inverse density, clipped to the range [0.2, 5] and normalized to mean 1. Pass these weights as sample_weight in the Ridge base fit and in XGBRegressor.fit for the residual model. The aim is to stop the dense central range of the target from dominating the L1 fit at the tails.
backlog.title: Target-density reweighting of training molecules

backlog.spec: Enlarge the linear base. After the standard scaling of the 7 physchem features (TPSA, MolLogP, HBD, HBA, MolWt, rotatable bonds, aromatic fraction), expand them with sklearn PolynomialFeatures(degree=2, include_bias=False) and standardize again. Fit Ridge with alpha chosen from [1, 10, 100] by an inner 3-fold KFold on the training data, using the seed argument for the split. Feed base predictions into the same XGBoost L1 residual model as before.
backlog.title: Degree-2 polynomial physchem base

backlog.spec: Replace the physchem Ridge base with a linear model on the fingerprint. Build X = log1p(Morgan count fingerprint, 2048 bits, radius 2) and fit Ridge(alpha=10) on it to predict y. Use out-of-fold predictions from an inner 5-fold KFold on the training set (seeded) as the base feature for the XGBoost L1 residual model, so the residual target is not leaked. For test molecules use the Ridge fitted on all training data. Keep the physchem features as extra XGBoost inputs.
backlog.title: Sparse linear fingerprint base instead of physchem ridge

backlog.spec: Replace the single L1 XGBoost fit with a two-pass robust fit. First fit XGBRegressor with reg:squarederror on the residual target r = y minus physchem base. Compute the training residuals e = r minus the in-sample prediction. Set sample weights w = 1/max(|e|, c) with c equal to the median absolute residual, and refit the XGBRegressor with reg:squarederror and these weights (same hyperparameters, random_state=seed). This approximates an L1 fit with iteratively reweighted least squares. Predict as before.
backlog.title: Robust IRLS-style reweighting of the boosted model

backlog.spec: Add a staged schedule to the XGBoost residual model. Stage 1: fit XGBRegressor(reg:absoluteerror) with n_estimators=200 on the 60 percent of training molecules with the smallest absolute physchem-base residual. Stage 2: continue training on all training molecules by passing the stage-1 model as xgb_model to fit (or refit with the same settings) for another 400 rounds with learning_rate 0.03. Keep all other hyperparameters unchanged, and use the seed argument for subsampling.
backlog.title: Easy-to-hard curriculum for the residual booster

backlog.spec: Keep the L1 XGBoost residual model but regularize the trees explicitly. Set reg_lambda=10 (L2 penalty on leaf weights), gamma=1.0 (minimum loss reduction per split), max_depth=4, min_child_weight=5, learning_rate=0.03 and n_estimators=900. Keep subsample=0.8 and colsample_bytree=0.3, and seed everything with random_state=seed. The goal is to test whether a smoother, shallower ensemble generalizes better across unseen scaffolds than the current deeper, lightly regularized trees.
backlog.title: Stronger leaf and split regularization in XGBoost

backlog.spec: Make the physchem base robust to scaffold clusters. Compute Murcko scaffolds of the training molecules and group them. Fit the Ridge base with sample weights 1/sqrt(size of the molecule's scaffold group), so that large scaffold families do not dominate the linear fit. Normalize the weights to mean 1. Then fit the XGBoost L1 residual model unchanged on the residual target. The aim is to make the linear trend follow the many distinct chemotypes rather than the few heavily represented ones.
backlog.title: Scaffold-holdout robust weighting of the physchem base

backlog.spec: Replace the stage-2 XGBoost L1 residual model with LightGBM using objective='l1', linear_tree=True, num_leaves=15, learning_rate=0.03, n_estimators=400, feature_fraction=0.3, bagging_fraction=0.8, bagging_freq=1, min_child_samples=5, random_state=seed. Keep the 200-round squared-error XGBoost stage 1 and the ridge physchem base unchanged. Fit LightGBM on the same training matrix and residuals y - base_tr. Piecewise-linear leaves let the booster extrapolate smooth trends such as logP and TPSA that constant leaves approximate poorly. Drop the features to only the Morgan counts and six physchem columns if LightGBM is slow on the full descriptor matrix.
backlog.title: LightGBM linear-tree residual booster

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace the Ridge physchem base with a pipeline of StandardScaler, then sklearn SplineTransformer(n_knots=5, degree=3, extrapolation='linear') applied to the 7 physchem features, then Ridge(alpha=3.0). Fit it on train physchem features and predict test as before. The residual XGBoost stages stay the same and consume base_tr and base_te. Splines give each physchem feature a smooth nonlinear shape without the explosion of pairwise terms seen with degree-2 polynomials.
backlog.title: Spline-expanded physchem base

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, for each Morgan bit that is active in at least 5 training molecules, compute a smoothed mean target: (sum of y over molecules with the bit + m * global_mean) / (count + m), with m=10. Compute these encodings out-of-fold within the training set using a 5-fold KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=seed) so that a training molecule never sees its own label. For test molecules, average the encodings of their active bits, taking the mean of the active bit encodings and the global mean where none are active. Add the per-molecule mean encoding and the encodings of the top 50 most-frequent bits as extra columns to the XGBoost matrix. The two-stage XGBoost residual model is otherwise unchanged.
backlog.title: Out-of-fold Bayesian target encoding of Morgan bits

backlog.spec: Compute Morgan bit-vector Tanimoto similarity between every molecule and the training set. For each molecule, append three features: the mean Tanimoto similarity to its 5 nearest training neighbours, the maximum similarity, and the mean target of those 5 neighbours. For training molecules, compute these out of fold with a 5-fold split, excluding the molecule itself and any molecule from its own fold, so the features are not leaked. Append the three columns to the XGBoost residual matrix. These features tell the booster how far a test molecule is from the training distribution, where the Murcko-scaffold split makes errors largest.
backlog.title: Applicability-domain similarity-density features

backlog.spec: Fit a quick XGBoost squared-error model (100 rounds, max_depth=4, colsample_bytree=0.5, random_state=seed) on the full featurized matrix. Keep only the top 60 RDKit descriptor columns by total gain plus all 2048 Morgan count columns, dropping the rest, and use this reduced matrix for both residual XGBoost stages. The selection uses only training labels, so it is valid inside fit_predict. The aim is to reduce the noise from weak descriptors that dilute column sampling, which is the dominant regularizer here.
backlog.title: Gain-based descriptor selection

backlog.spec: Replace the single Ridge physchem base with an average of 10 Ridge(alpha=1.0) fits, each trained on a bootstrap resample of the training molecules drawn with np.random.default_rng(seed + k). Average the 10 predictions on both train and test to form base_tr and base_te. Keep the two-stage XGBoost residual pipeline unchanged. Bagging smooths the linear base, whose coefficients can vary across folds of scaffolds, and reduces variance in the residuals that the booster must fit.
backlog.title: Bootstrap-bagged physchem base

backlog.spec: Keep the current two-stage XGBoost model, but pass feature_weights to XGBoost's fit for both stages. Give the 6 physchem columns and the aromatic-fraction column a weight of 4.0 and every fingerprint column a weight of 1.0. Set colsample_bynode=0.3 with colsample_bytree=1.0 so that each split draws its candidate features with probability proportional to these weights. This keeps the fingerprint diversity while making the physchem descriptors appear in more splits. Use DMatrix-level feature_weights with the same random_state=seed.
backlog.title: Column-weighted sampling that favours physchem features

backlog.spec: Before the two-stage fit, replicate the training matrix 3 times. In the copies, add Gaussian noise with standard deviation 0.05 to the residual targets y - base_tr, using np.random.default_rng(seed). Keep the original copy unjittered and stack all copies into one XGBoost training set. Use the same two-stage schedule (200 squared-error rounds, then 400 L1 rounds). This acts as a smoothing regularizer on the target, a different mechanism from matrix replication and from mixup, and it should soften the fit to individual noisy labels.
backlog.title: Label-jitter augmentation for the residual booster

backlog.spec: Cluster the training molecules with rdkit.ML.Cluster.Butina at a Tanimoto distance threshold of 0.6 on Morgan bit fingerprints. Then train 5 two-stage XGBoost residual models, each excluding one random cluster-group of about 20 percent of the training molecules, with random_state=seed+k. Average their test predictions, and keep the ridge physchem base as is. Leaving out whole chemical clusters forces each member to generalise across chemotypes, which mimics the scaffold-held-out test condition more closely than random bagging.
backlog.title: Within-train Butina-cluster leave-out ensemble

backlog.spec: Keep the 200-round squared-error XGBoost stage 1. For stage 2, train two models from the same stage-1 booster: one with reg:absoluteerror for 400 rounds as now, and one with reg:squarederror for 400 rounds. Return base_te + 0.75 * L1_prediction + 0.25 * L2_prediction on the test set. The squared-error head reduces variance in the bulk of the residuals, while the L1 head keeps the median-type robustness that matches the MAE metric. Use the same learning rate and colsample settings for both heads.
backlog.title: Blended L1 and L2 stage-two objectives

backlog.spec: Keep the current two-stage XGBoost model and physchem ridge base unchanged. In featurize_one, after the Morgan count vector, compute BRICS fragments with rdkit.Chem.BRICS.BRICSDecompose(m) and hash each fragment SMILES into 512 count bins with a stable hash (e.g. zlib.crc32 modulo 512). Append these 512 counts to the feature vector (float32). Everything else, including the cache and the seed handling, stays the same.
backlog.title: BRICS fragment count features

backlog.spec: Keep the current pipeline. In featurize_one, use rdkit.Chem.rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs(m) (or rdMolDescriptors.GetCrippenContribs) to get the Crippen logP atom type for each heavy atom. Count occurrences of each Crippen atom type across the train and test set vocabulary (build the vocabulary from training molecules only, keep unseen types dropped) and append these counts plus the summed Crippen logP and summed molar refractivity to the features. Use the same features for the physchem ridge base as an added 2-column input.
backlog.title: Crippen atom-type contribution counts

backlog.spec: Add a fixed, seeded random-feature graph convolution as an extra feature block. For each molecule, build a per-atom feature vector (one-hot element among C,N,O,S,F,Cl,Br,other; degree; formal charge; aromatic flag; total H count), scale to unit norm. Draw a fixed random matrix W (feature dim by 64) and a fixed random matrix V (64 by 64) from numpy RandomState(0) with variance 1/dim, and iterate H <- tanh(A_norm @ H @ V + H @ W_self) for 3 hops, where A_norm is the row-normalized adjacency with self-loops. Sum-pool the atom states per molecule into a 64-dim vector per hop and concatenate the three hop embeddings (192 dims) to the Morgan plus descriptor features. No learned parameters, so no leakage across folds; the boosted model learns from them.
backlog.title: Random-feature graph convolution embedding

backlog.spec: Replace the stage-two L1 fit with a stacked model. Inside fit_predict, split the training set into 3 inner folds (KFold, shuffle, random_state=seed). For each inner fold, fit the stage-one squared-error XGBoost (200 rounds) on the other two folds and record pred_leaf=True leaf indices on the held-out fold and on the test molecules. Build one-hot encodings of the leaf indices (sklearn OneHotEncoder with handle_unknown='ignore') and fit a Ridge(alpha=1.0) on [leaf one-hots, scaled physchem features] to the residual y - base_tr using the out-of-fold rows. Predict test residuals with the leaf encodings from the full stage-one model averaged with the inner-fold models. Final prediction is base_te plus the ridge output. Use the seed argument for all randomness.
backlog.title: Leaf-embedding stacking of stage-one trees

backlog.spec: Add out-of-fold auxiliary features derived from physical descriptors. For the training set, compute the six RDKit descriptors MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors and NumRotatableBonds. Using 5-fold KFold (shuffle, random_state=seed) inside the training set, predict each of these six descriptors from the 2048-bit Morgan bit vector with Ridge(alpha=10) and record out-of-fold predictions for the training rows. For the test molecules, fit each Ridge on all training molecules and predict. Append these 6 predicted descriptor values as extra columns to the XGBoost input (both stages). The true descriptors remain in the physchem base only, so the boosted model sees learned fingerprint-to-property estimates that generalize across scaffolds.
backlog.title: Auxiliary descriptor-prediction stacking features

backlog.spec: Keep the two-stage XGBoost L1 pipeline. Build a monotone_constraints tuple of length equal to the feature count: 0 for every Morgan column and 0 for every RDKit descriptor column except MolLogP (+1) and TPSA (-1), located by their index in Descriptors.descList. Pass monotone_constraints to both XGBRegressor stages through params (tree_method='hist' already supports it). Physical intuition is that permeability rises with lipophilicity and falls with polar surface area, and the constraint regularizes the trees without changing the feature set.
backlog.title: Monotone constraints on lipophilicity and polarity in XGBoost

backlog.spec: Replace the single stage-two L1 model with two XGBoost L1 experts (same params, 400 rounds each, after the existing 200-round squared-error stage one). Expert A trains on training molecules with MolWt below the training median and expert B on the rest. At prediction time, compute a soft gate g = sigmoid((MolWt - median)/s) with s equal to the training MolWt standard deviation divided by 4, and return base_te + (1-g)*A(x) + g*B(x) for test molecules. Both experts start from the same stage-one booster. This is a bold architecture change that lets the residual model specialize across molecular size.
backlog.title: Molecular-weight gated mixture of two L1 experts

backlog.spec: Add charge-based descriptors to the feature vector. In featurize_one, call rdkit.Chem.rdPartialCharges.ComputeGasteigerCharges(m) and read the '_GasteigerCharge' property of each heavy atom, ignoring NaN values. Compute: maximum partial charge, minimum partial charge, sum of positive charges, sum of negative charges, the count of atoms with absolute charge above 0.25, and the charge-weighted surface proxy sum over heavy atoms of |charge| times the atom's TPSA contribution from rdMolDescriptors._CalcTPSAContribs. Append these six values to the feature vector and to the physchem ridge base input. Charges are computed per molecule, so there is no leakage.
backlog.title: Gasteiger partial-charge surface descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the single radius-2 Morgan count vector with a multi-scale concatenation. Compute three count fingerprints with GetMorganGenerator: radius 1 with 1024 bits, radius 2 with 2048 bits (current), and radius 3 with 2048 bits, each hashed separately and each taken as counts. Concatenate them into one 5120-column block before the RDKit descriptors. Keep the two-stage XGBoost L1 model and the physchem ridge base unchanged. Set colsample_bytree to 0.2 to keep the per-tree feature budget similar to the current setting, because the input is now larger.
backlog.title: Multi-radius Morgan count features

backlog.spec: Keep the two-stage pipeline, the features and the physchem base unchanged. In stage two, replace objective='reg:absoluteerror' with objective='reg:quantileerror' and set quantile_alpha=0.5 (the median, which is the same target as MAE but implemented through the quantile-loss path with its own leaf-value update). Keep xgb_model=stage1.get_booster() warm start and 400 rounds. Use the seed argument as random_state. This is a small optimizer-family swap to check whether the quantile leaf update fits the median target better than the absolute-error leaf update.
backlog.title: XGBoost quantile objective for the median stage

backlog.spec: Before the XGBoost stages, fit an sklearn MLPRegressor autoencoder (hidden sizes 256, 32, 256, identity output, early stopping) that reconstructs standardized RDKit descriptors concatenated with the Morgan count vector. Fit it on the stacked train and test feature matrices, which is unsupervised and transductive, and use a fixed seed. Take the 32-unit bottleneck activations (via a manual forward pass over the fitted coefs_ and intercepts_) and append them to Xtr and Xte. Keep the existing ridge physchem base and the two-stage XGBoost L1 residual model unchanged.
backlog.title: Unsupervised autoencoder bottleneck features

backlog.spec: Keep the existing two-stage XGBoost residual model, but use it as a adaptive kernel. For each test molecule, find the leaf it lands in for every tree (booster.predict with pred_leaf=True). Weight each training molecule by the number of trees in which it shares a leaf with the test molecule, normalized. Predict the test value as base_te plus the weighted median of the training residuals (y minus base_tr), using the weights. This aligns the aggregation with the MAE objective instead of the mean of the leaf values. Use the same training data for the kernel as for the residuals.
backlog.title: Boosted-leaf kernel weighted median

backlog.spec: Replace the global ridge physchem base with a local model. Standardize the 7 physchem features using training statistics. For each test molecule, take the k=60 nearest training molecules in that standardized space, with weights from a Gaussian kernel of distance (bandwidth set to the median neighbour distance). Fit a weighted linear regression with a small ridge penalty on those neighbours and predict the test value. Use this local prediction as base_te and base_tr (base_tr via leave-one-out neighbours) in place of the global Ridge base, and keep the XGBoost residual stages on top.
backlog.title: Local weighted-median regression in physchem space

backlog.spec: Replace the depth-6 trees in both XGBoost residual stages with depth-1 trees (max_depth=1, which gives a boosted additive model with no interactions). Use squared-error for the first 200 rounds at learning_rate 0.05, then switch to reg:absoluteerror for 600 rounds on the same matrix, continuing from the first booster as before. The first-stage rounds may need a larger learning rate because stumps learn more slowly. Keep colsample_bytree 0.3 and subsample 0.8. The point is to test whether interaction terms are the source of overfitting across scaffolds.
backlog.title: Depth-one additive boosting for the residual stage

backlog.spec: Replace the Ridge physchem base with a robust linear fit solved by iteratively reweighted least squares. Start from the Ridge solution. At each of about 20 iterations, compute residuals on the training set, set a scale from the median absolute deviation (times 1.4826), and set weights w = 1/(1+(r/c)^2) with tuning constant c = 1.5 times that scale. Refit a weighted ridge (alpha=1.0) with those weights and stop when coefficients change by less than 1e-6. Use the fitted coefficients for base_tr and base_te, and keep the XGBoost residual stages unchanged.
backlog.title: Cauchy-loss IRLS physchem base

backlog.spec: Fit the StandardScaler used for the physchem base on the stacked train and test physchem matrices, not on train alone. This is unsupervised and uses only the SMILES, not labels. Keep the Ridge fit on train rows only, so the change affects only the scaling of the inputs. Also clip the standardized values of each physchem feature to the range [-4, 4] to limit the influence of outlier test molecules on the linear base. Everything else, including the two-stage XGBoost residual model, stays the same.
backlog.title: Transductive physchem standardization

backlog.spec: Before fitting the physchem Ridge and the residual stages, divide the training target by a size factor s = sqrt(number of heavy atoms) (computed per molecule, so the target becomes y/s). Fit the Ridge base and both XGBoost stages on the scaled target y/s, then at prediction time multiply the combined output by s of each test molecule. Physchem features and the Morgan fingerprint stay unchanged. This tests whether the variance of the log permeability depends on molecule size and whether the MAE trees fit better on a scaled target.
backlog.title: Target rescaling by molecular size

backlog.spec: Augment the stage-2 training set by stacking two copies of the training matrix. In the second copy, add Gaussian noise with standard deviation 0.1 times the column standard deviation to the continuous RDKit descriptor columns only, and leave the fingerprint columns unchanged. Keep the labels and residuals as they are. Fit stage 2 on the stacked matrix (1456 rows) with reg:absoluteerror and the same learning rate and number of rounds, and keep the stage-1 model as before. The noise is a smoothing regularizer on the continuous descriptors, not on the labels.
backlog.title: Descriptor-jitter augmentation for the residual booster

backlog.spec: Keep the stage-1 squared-error XGBoost model. Train three stage-2 L1 models starting from the same stage-1 booster, each with a different seed and a different random 50% partition of the columns made available to the model through feature_weights (set to 1 for the chosen columns and 0.2 for the rest). Average their residual predictions with the mean. The aim is to reduce variance from the column sampling without the cost of a full bagged ensemble. Keep the physchem ridge base and all other settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Seed-diverse stage-two averaging with different column partitions

backlog.spec: Choose the number of stage-1 squared-error rounds on the training data only, without touching the test fold. Split the training molecules into 4 groups by Murcko scaffold (GroupKFold on scaffold keys). Train the stage-1 model once for 400 rounds on three groups and record the validation MAE of the residual predictions at 50-round intervals, using the fold's training residuals. Pick the round count with the lowest validation MAE (restricted to 100 to 300 rounds), then refit the stage-1 model on all training data with that count and continue with the existing stage-2 L1 model unchanged.
backlog.title: Stage-one early stopping by inner scaffold holdout

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, before the final fit, run a small random search (about 12 draws) over stage-2 XGBoost settings: max_depth in {3,4,5,6,8}, colsample_bytree in {0.1,0.2,0.3,0.5}, min_child_weight in {1,3,8}, learning_rate in {0.02,0.03,0.05}, and subsample in {0.6,0.8,1.0}. Score each draw by a 3-fold GroupKFold on train_smiles, grouping rows by Murcko scaffold, using MAE on the residual target y - base_tr. Refit the two-stage model (stage 1 squared error 200 rounds, stage 2 absolute error 400 rounds) with the best draw. Use seed for the sampler and the model. Keep the physchem ridge base unchanged.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped random search for stage-2 XGBoost settings

backlog.spec: Keep the existing radius-2 count fingerprint and descriptor matrix. Add a dense sketch of the count fingerprint: draw a fixed random sign matrix of shape (2048, 256) with entries +1 or -1 from np.random.default_rng(seed), scale by 1/sqrt(256), and multiply it with the log1p-transformed Morgan counts. Append the 256 projected columns to the XGBoost input for both stages. The projection depends only on seed, so it is identical for train and test rows. Leave all other settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Johnson-Lindenstrauss random-sign projection of Morgan counts

backlog.spec: Replace the hashed 2048-bit Morgan count vector with collision-free environment counts. Generate radius-1 to radius-3 Morgan environments with bitInfo (or the unfolded atom-environment identifiers) for each training molecule. Keep only environments that occur in at least 5 training molecules, and count them per molecule. Learn the kept vocabulary from the training fold only, and drop unseen environments at test time. Feed these columns, plus the existing descriptors, to the unchanged two-stage XGBoost residual model.
backlog.title: Unhashed frequent-substructure count features

backlog.spec: Create one extra feature for the boosted stage: the Tanimoto-similarity-weighted mean of the training targets of each molecule's 10 nearest training neighbours. For the training rows, compute this out-of-fold with an inner 5-fold GroupKFold on Murcko scaffolds, so that a molecule never uses its own target or same-scaffold neighbours. For test rows, use all training molecules. Append the feature as one column to the XGBoost input for both stages. Use bit-vector Tanimoto from the Morgan bits.
backlog.title: Out-of-fold Tanimoto-kNN target feature for the boosted model

backlog.spec: Replace the stage-2 XGBoost call with a hand-written gradient-boosting loop on the residual target r = y - base_tr. Start from the median of r. In each of 300 rounds, compute the sign of the residual, fit a sklearn DecisionTreeRegressor (max_depth 5, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 3, random_state=seed) to the sign, and then reset each leaf value to the median of the actual residuals in that leaf. Add the tree to the prediction with shrinkage 0.05. Keep stage 1 as the squared-error XGBoost fit. Use this L1 learner for stage 2.
backlog.title: Median-leaf gradient boosting with exact L1 leaf renewal

backlog.spec: After the two-stage model produces predictions for the test molecules, apply a monotone quantile mapping. Compute the training-target quantiles at 101 evenly spaced levels from train_y, and compute the same quantile levels of the model's predictions on the training rows, using out-of-fold predictions from an inner 5-fold GroupKFold on scaffolds. Map each test prediction through the piecewise-linear function from prediction quantile to target quantile, with np.interp and clipping at the ends. This corrects compression of the spread that the MAE-trained model shows. Use it only if the inner-fold MAE improves.
backlog.title: Quantile remapping of predictions to the training target distribution

backlog.spec: Before the physchem ridge, build a small set of nonlinear features from the physchem vector. Run a tiny genetic-programming search over expressions built from the 7 physchem columns (TPSA, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, MolWt, NumRotatableBonds, aromatic fraction) using +, -, *, safe division, log1p(abs), and sqrt(abs). Use population 60 for 15 generations, with fitness equal to inner 3-fold GroupKFold MAE of a Ridge fit on the training rows, and keep the best 6 expressions. Append them to the standardized physchem features before the ridge base. Seed all random choices with seed.
backlog.title: Symbolic feature construction on physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: Build a small directed message-passing network in plain numpy. Give each atom a one-hot vector for element, degree, aromaticity, and H count, and make a 64-dimensional embedding. Run 3 rounds of message passing over directed bonds, with messages from the neighbours passed through a learned linear map and tanh. Sum-pool to a molecular vector. Train a linear readout head with Adam (learning rate 0.01, weight decay 1e-4, 300 full-batch steps) on the training rows with L1 loss on the residual y - base_tr. Initialise from np.random.default_rng(seed). Append the 64-dimensional pooled embedding, computed from the learned weights, as extra columns to the XGBoost input. Keep the molecule-level cache so each SMILES is parsed once.
backlog.title: Numpy directed message-passing embedding as an extra feature

backlog.spec: In the physchem block, replace StandardScaler with robust scaling. Compute the column median and interquartile range from the training rows only, and divide by the IQR (fall back to 1 where the IQR is 0). Apply the same transform to the test rows. Keep Ridge(alpha=1.0) and the rest of the two-stage XGBoost residual model unchanged. This limits the influence of extreme MolWt and TPSA values on the linear base, which the current mean/SD scaling does not do.
backlog.title: Robust median and IQR scaling for the physchem base

backlog.spec: Keep the two-stage XGBoost residual model, but average the stage-2 predictions over 5 fits. Each fit uses seed+k for k in 0..4, and each fit restricts colsample to a different fixed random partition of the feature columns (half of the columns, drawn from rng(seed+k)). Average the five test predictions with equal weights. Do not change the stage-1 fit, which is shared. This is a cheap variance reduction on the stage-2 MAE fit.
backlog.title: Stage-two seed ensemble with column partitions

backlog.spec: Keep the current physchem ridge base and two-stage XGBoost. Add a sparse feature block built from the raw canonical SMILES string: character n-grams with n in {2,3,4} (use a simple Python counter over substrings, no sklearn text vectorizer needed), keep only n-grams that occur in at least 5 training molecules, apply sublinear TF weighting and L2 row normalization, and scale to the scale of the other features. Append these columns to the Morgan-plus-descriptor matrix before both XGBoost stages. Fit the vocabulary on the training fold only; ignore unseen n-grams at test time.
backlog.title: SMILES character n-gram TF-IDF features

backlog.spec: Keep everything as in the incumbent, but add a parallel base model. Take log1p of the 2048-bit Morgan count vector, standardize it, and map it through 1024 random Fourier features cos(Wx+b) with W drawn Gaussian (scale chosen so the median pairwise distance gives a bandwidth of about 1) and b uniform on [0, 2pi], using a seed-dependent RNG. Fit a Ridge(alpha tuned in {1,10,100} by inner scaffold-grouped validation on the training fold) on these features to predict y minus the physchem base. Use its predictions on train (in-sample) and test as an extra XGBoost input column. This approximates a Gaussian kernel ridge without the O(n^2) cost.
backlog.title: Random Fourier features of Morgan counts as a kernel base

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, first train 5 copies of the two-stage residual model on bootstrap samples of the training fold (seed+k), and produce out-of-bag predictions for each training molecule by averaging only copies that did not see it. Replace the training targets with a 50/50 blend of the true y and these out-of-bag ensemble predictions, then fit the final single two-stage XGBoost model on the blended targets. At test time predict with that single model only. The aim is a smoother target that reduces the influence of noisy labels while keeping one model's cost at prediction time.
backlog.title: Distill a bagged out-of-fold ensemble into one booster

backlog.spec: Keep the two-stage XGBoost L1 model and features unchanged, but change the regularization of the tree building. Set max_bin=32 (coarser split candidates for the sparse count features) and colsample_bynode=0.5 in addition to the existing colsample_bytree=0.3, and keep all other parameters the same. The coarse bins and per-split feature sampling together act as a structural regularizer on the many sparse Morgan columns. Do not change the number of rounds.
backlog.title: Coarse histogram bins with per-node column sampling

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan count generator with one that sees more atom information: pass useChirality=True to the Morgan generator and, using an atom-invariant function you write, add ring membership (in ring, smallest ring size bucket 3-4/5-6/7+) to the invariants so that substructures are distinguished by ring context. Keep radius 2 and 2048 bits and count folding as before. Concatenate the resulting count vector with the existing RDKit descriptors. The change keeps the feature dimension fixed and only alters which substructures collide.
backlog.title: Chirality- and ring-aware Morgan invariants

backlog.spec: In both XGBoost stages replace the uniform subsample=0.8 with stratified row sampling. Split training rows into 5 quantile bins of the current residual target (computed on the stage input y minus base), and within each bin draw 80 percent of rows without replacement for each boosting round. Implement this by building a per-round row mask and passing it through a custom loop with xgb.train on a DMatrix, or by refitting XGBoost in 20-round chunks with a fresh mask each chunk and warm-starting from the booster. Everything else (depth, learning rate, rounds, L1 stage-two objective) stays the same.
backlog.title: Quantile-stratified row subsampling per tree

backlog.spec: Add a bit-based linear base before the XGBoost stages. Binarize the Morgan count vector (count > 0). Compute a sign target by thresholding the training labels at their median and form a log-count ratio r_j = log((p_j+1)/|P|) - log((q_j+1)/|Q|) on the binarized features, where p_j and q_j are feature occurrence counts among high and low molecules. Multiply each binarized feature by r_j and fit a Ridge(alpha=10) on the scaled features to predict y minus the physchem base. Feed its in-sample and test predictions as one extra column to the XGBoost stages. Compute r_j inside fit_predict on the training fold only.
backlog.title: NB-SVM log-count-ratio fingerprint base

backlog.spec: Change only the stage-one objective. Replace reg:squarederror with reg:pseudohubererror and set huber_slope equal to 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of the stage-one residual (y minus physchem base) on the training fold, computed once before fitting. Keep stage two (L1 absolute-error, 400 rounds, starting from the stage-one booster) and all other settings unchanged. This gives a robust start for the residual model that scales with the noise level of the training fold instead of relying on squared error.
backlog.title: Huber stage one with per-stage MAD scale

backlog.spec: Before fitting, compute for each training molecule a complexity proxy: the number of ring systems in its Murcko scaffold plus the number of rotatable bonds, normalized by the training-fold mean. Fit the physchem ridge base on the targets divided by a per-molecule scale s_i = 1 + 0.25 * (complexity_i - mean), then multiply test-time base predictions by the same test-molecule scale. Train both XGBoost stages on the rescaled residuals (y/s minus base) and multiply the final predictions by s_test. This is a multiplicative size correction that lets the residual model work on comparable targets across scaffold sizes.
backlog.title: Scaffold-complexity target scaling

backlog.spec: Keep the two-stage model, but make the stage-two learning rate taper across boosting rounds rather than being constant. Train stage two in 4 chunks of 100 rounds using xgb_model warm start, setting learning_rate to 0.03, 0.02, 0.012, and 0.006 respectively for the chunks (stage one stays at 0.03). Keep reg:absoluteerror and all other parameters. This is a simple decreasing schedule inside the L1 stage to reduce overfitting at the end of the boost, and it needs no extra data split.
backlog.title: Per-round learning-rate taper inside a single booster

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace the Ridge(alpha=1.0) physchem base with sklearn ARDRegression (default priors, max_iter=300) fit on the StandardScaler-transformed physchem features concatenated with the Morgan count columns that are nonzero in at least 5 training molecules (log1p-transformed). Use its predictions as base_tr and base_te exactly as the Ridge base is used now; the two XGBoost residual stages stay unchanged. Automatic relevance determination prunes weak fingerprint bits and gives a sparse Bayesian linear base, a family not yet tried for the base.
backlog.title: Sparse Bayesian ARD linear base replacing physchem Ridge

backlog.spec: Replace the physchem Ridge base with a second-order factorization machine trained in numpy on the training fold only: prediction = w0 + w.x + sum_{i<j} <v_i, v_j> x_i x_j, with x = standardized physchem features plus binary Morgan presence bits (columns present in at least 5 training molecules), latent rank k=8, L2 penalty 1e-3 on weights and factors, full-batch Adam for about 300 steps at learning rate 0.01, initialized with small random factors from the seed. Use its output as base_tr and base_te and keep the two XGBoost residual stages. The FM learns pairwise substructure interactions that a linear base cannot.
backlog.title: Factorization-machine base model

backlog.spec: Before the XGBoost stages, fit sklearn PLSRegression (n_components=8) on the log1p Morgan count matrix against the training targets. To avoid leakage, produce the training-row PLS scores out-of-fold with an inner 5-fold KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=seed) and fit a full-train PLS for the test rows. Append the 8 PLS score columns to the feature matrix of both XGBoost residual stages. Unlike the earlier truncated SVD, these components are target-supervised.
backlog.title: Supervised PLS components as extra features

backlog.spec: Replace the two XGBoost residual stages with a manual boosting loop of 150 rounds on the residual y - base_tr. Each round: randomly partition the standardized feature columns into 10 disjoint subsets, for each subset fit a PCA rotation on a bootstrap (70%) of the training rows, rotate that subset, and stack all rotated blocks into a matrix; fit a single sklearn DecisionTreeRegressor (max_depth=5, min_samples_leaf=10, criterion='absolute_error' only if speed allows, else squared_error) on the current residual; add 0.1 times its prediction to the running model. The per-round rotations and bootstraps use the seed. Predict test rows by replaying the same rotations. This adds rotation diversity that gradient boosting on raw columns lacks.
backlog.title: Rotation-forest boosting for the residual stage

backlog.spec: Build a graph over all training and test molecules (train plus test SMILES) with edge weights equal to the Tanimoto similarity of their Morgan bit vectors, keeping only the 10 strongest neighbours per node and zeroing the rest. Run standard label spreading (Zhou et al., alpha=0.8, 30 iterations of F <- alpha*S*F + (1-alpha)*Y0) with the training targets clamped in Y0 and zeros for test rows, where S is the symmetrically normalized kernel. Use the spread values at the test rows, minus their mean, as one extra column (and the same for training rows computed with that row's own label excluded, via leave-one-out by zeroing its diagonal) added to the XGBoost feature matrix. Test molecules contribute to the graph structure, not to any label.
backlog.title: Transductive label spreading on a Tanimoto graph

backlog.spec: Use rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize Uncharger to create a neutralized version of every SMILES that has formal charges. In featurize, cache features for both the original and neutralized SMILES. Train the XGBoost residual model on the stacked rows (original rows plus neutralized copies of charged molecules, with the same target), and at prediction time return the average of the predictions for the original SMILES and its neutralized form (when they differ; otherwise the single prediction). Charged groups in Caco-2 data are ionization-sensitive, so this augmentation and averaging is a test-time ensemble over protonation-like variants, not a reordering of the existing standardization idea.
backlog.title: Charge-state augmentation with test-time neutral averaging

backlog.spec: After the physchem Ridge base, fit a RandomForestRegressor (300 trees, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=5, random_state=seed) on the log1p Morgan counts plus physchem features, with target y - base_tr. For each test molecule, compute the leaf co-membership weights against all training molecules (average over trees of 1/leaf-size for shared leaves), then predict base_te plus the weighted median of the training residuals under those weights (a quantile-regression-forest style estimate). This gives a nonparametric conditional-median residual correction, distinct from boosted-leaf kernels, and the L1 median suits the MAE metric.
backlog.title: Random-forest proximity-weighted median of residuals

backlog.spec: Replace the two-stage XGBoost residual model with a hand-written NGBoost-style booster that models the residual as Laplace(location mu, log-scale s). Initialize mu and s from the training residual median and log-MAD. For 300 rounds, compute the Laplace negative-log-likelihood gradients with respect to mu and s, rescale them by the inverse Fisher information (for Laplace, mu-scale 1/b^2 and s-scale 1 in the natural parametrization), fit a shallow XGBoost regressor (max_depth=4, 60 trees, learning_rate 0.1) to each natural gradient, and update mu and s with step 0.05. Predict the location mu for test molecules and add it to base_te. Optimizing the Laplace likelihood is the principled median-consistent objective, and natural-gradient steps are a family not tried yet.
backlog.title: Laplace-likelihood natural-gradient booster (NGBoost-style)

backlog.spec: Split the residual-correction stage into two heads. First, fit an XGBoost classifier (objective binary:logistic, 200 trees, max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.05) predicting whether the residual y - base_tr is positive. Second, fit the existing XGBoost reg:absoluteerror regressor on the residual magnitude |y - base_tr| restricted to the training rows, and also a reg:absoluteerror regressor on the signed residual. At prediction time, compute the probability p of a positive residual and output base_te + (2p-1)*m, where m is the predicted magnitude from the absolute-residual head clipped to be nonnegative. This is a hurdle-style decomposition of the correction into sign and size, unlike the current single signed L1 fit.
backlog.title: Residual-sign gate with L1 magnitude head

backlog.spec: In featurize_one, after computing the radius-2 Morgan count vector, multiply each count column by an inverse-document-frequency weight idf_j = log((1+N)/(1+df_j)) + 1, where N is the number of training molecules and df_j is the number of training molecules with a nonzero count in column j. Compute df once per fit_predict call from the training SMILES (test SMILES only enter through the same fixed weights), apply the same weights to test molecules, and then take log1p of the weighted counts before concatenating the physchem descriptors. Down-weighting common substructures and up-weighting rare ones changes the tree split geometry without adding columns.
backlog.title: IDF-weighted Morgan count transform

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute the Murcko generic scaffold of every training and test molecule. For training rows, build an out-of-fold encoding: split the training set into 5 scaffold-grouped inner folds, and for each inner fold compute, from the other folds only, the mean residual y - base_tr per generic scaffold, shrunk toward zero with an empirical-Bayes weight n/(n+k), k=5. Test rows get the same shrunk mean computed from all training rows, with unseen scaffolds set to 0. Append this single column (plus the scaffold's training count) to the Morgan+descriptor matrix before both XGBoost stages. Everything else stays the same.
backlog.title: Scaffold-level empirical-Bayes target encoding

backlog.spec: Keep the two-stage XGBoost residual model unchanged except for stage 2. Set grow_policy='lossguide', max_leaves=31, max_depth=0 and keep objective='reg:absoluteerror', n_estimators=400, and the same learning rate and subsampling. Leaf-wise best-first growth lets the L1 model spend its splits where the absolute-error gain is largest, rather than growing every branch to a fixed depth. Keep stage 1 depth-wise at max_depth=6.
backlog.title: Lossguide tree growth for the stage-2 L1 model

backlog.spec: In stage 1, fit one XGBoost model on a multi-target matrix: the main target (y - base_tr) plus the standardized values of TPSA, MolLogP, MolWt and NumHDonors, which are computed from training molecules only. Use tree_method='hist' with multi_strategy='multi_output_tree' (or the closest available multi-target option in the installed xgboost version; fall back to a single-target fit if it is unavailable). The auxiliary columns force shared splits that encode physicochemical structure into the trees. Use only the first output column as the residual prediction for test molecules. Stage 2 is the L1 model on the main target residual, unchanged.
