backlog.title: Multi-output trees with auxiliary physchem targets

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed Ridge(alpha=1.0) physchem base with a choice of alpha among {0.1, 1, 10, 100}. Pick alpha by a scaffold-grouped inner 4-fold CV on the training set, minimizing mean absolute error of the Ridge predictions. Use GroupKFold on Murcko scaffold strings, with the group labels derived from the training molecules only. Refit Ridge on all training data with the chosen alpha, then run the rest of the two-stage XGBoost residual model unchanged.
backlog.title: Cross-validated Ridge strength for the physchem base

backlog.spec: Before the StandardScaler in the physchem base, apply sklearn PowerTransformer(method='yeo-johnson', standardize=True) fit on the training physchem rows only (MolWt, TPSA, MolLogP, HBD, HBA, rotatable bonds, aromatic fraction). Use the same transformer on test rows. Fit the Ridge(alpha=1.0) base on the transformed features and keep the residual XGBoost two-stage model unchanged. This removes skew in MolWt and TPSA so the linear base is not dominated by a few large molecules.
backlog.title: Yeo-Johnson power transform before the physchem base

backlog.spec: Replace the linear Ridge physchem base with KernelRidge(kernel='rbf', alpha=1.0, gamma=1/7) on the standardized 7 physchem features, fit on the training rows only, with the target centered by the training mean before fitting and the mean added back at prediction time. The base predictions on the training rows are used to form the residuals for the two-stage XGBoost model, exactly as in the current script. This gives a nonlinear smooth base that captures the known curvature of permeability against TPSA without adding fingerprint noise.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge with RBF kernel as the physchem base

backlog.spec: Replace the linear base with a cascade. Stage 0: fit a shallow XGBoost (squared error, max_depth=3, 200 rounds, lr 0.03) on the 7 physchem features only, using y. Stage 1 and stage 2 are then the current two-stage XGBoost residual model on Morgan+descriptor features, fit on y minus the stage-0 in-sample predictions. Predict test rows as stage-0 prediction plus the stage-1 and stage-2 contributions. The point of the cascade is that the physchem interactions are learned by a small, well-regularized model, and the fingerprint model only corrects what remains.
backlog.title: Cascade: physchem-only booster before the Morgan residual

backlog.spec: In featurize_one, build the molecule with Chem.AddHs before computing the Morgan count fingerprint with radius 2 and 2048 bits, so that hydrogen-bearing environments are counted. Keep the RDKit descriptor block computed on the original (no explicit H) molecule, so the descriptors are unchanged. Keep the current two-stage XGBoost residual model unchanged. The aim is to test whether explicit-H environments give the trees more information about donor and acceptor patterns that matter for Caco-2 transport.
backlog.title: Explicit-hydrogen atom-environment counts

backlog.spec: Keep the two-stage model. In stage 2, instead of a constant learning rate, train with a two-phase schedule using the xgboost training API on a DMatrix. Use learning_rate 0.08 for the first 60 rounds, then 0.02 for the next 340 rounds, and keep objective='reg:absoluteerror' with the same subsampling and depth. Implement by training 60 rounds, then continuing from the booster with the new learning rate set via booster parameter updates. The larger early step moves the L1 model quickly away from the squared-error starting point, and the smaller later steps smooth the final fit.
backlog.title: Two-speed learning-rate schedule in stage 2

backlog.spec: Keep the two-stage model, but output a mixture: pred = w * (base_te + stage2_pred) + (1 - w) * base_te, equivalent to shrinking the booster correction by w. Choose w from {0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25} by scaffold-grouped inner 4-fold CV on the training set, minimizing the mean absolute error of the out-of-fold predictions. Refit the full model on all training rows and apply the chosen w to the test correction. This is a single scalar correction that tests whether the booster is over- or under-confident on new scaffolds, and it costs one extra fit per inner fold.
backlog.title: Blend the physchem base and the full model by inner CV weight

incumbent.description: Fit the XGBoost residual model in two stages: 200 rounds of squared-error boosting, then 400 more rounds continued from that booster with absolute-error (L1) loss, keeping all other hyperparameters as in the incumbent.

memo:
Helped: structural changes to the residual setup. XGBoost L1 replacing the random forest gave 0.3828, down from 0.4417. A physchem ridge base with XGBoost on its residuals gave 0.3755/0.3715. Two-stage XGBoost (squared error, then L1) gave 0.3658/0.3652, the incumbent.

Did not help, or was within noise (sd about 0.0037): other model families (LightGBM 0.3830, CatBoost 0.3860, GP 0.3859, MLP 0.4962, kernel methods), ensembles and bagging (0.3793, 0.3795), extra fingerprints (Avalon+ErG 0.3710, atom-pair/torsion 0.3689), 3D shape 0.3760, calibration 0.3745, ridge-base variants (polynomial 0.3940, sparse L1 0.3882, spline 0.3763), heavier regularization 0.3725, monotone constraints 0.3697, winsorizing 0.3727, NGBoost-style 0.3733.

Small gains near noise: collision-free Morgan radius 0-3 (0.3625), feature_weights (0.3642), applicability-domain features (0.3646), multi-radius Morgan (0.3646).

Next: combine those four on the two-stage fit and replicate before accepting. Vary stage round counts and learning rate. Avoid specs that abort at the engine.
